name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee Sewri–Nhava Sheva Atal Setu
lanes: 6 lanes (3 each way), sea bridge with viaduct approaches

route.end: Chirle (near Nhava Sheva), Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra

timeline.event: Inaugurated on 12 January and opened to traffic

history: Atal Setu is a giant bridge across Mumbai's harbour, connecting Sewri in the island city with Chirle on the Navi Mumbai side. Planned for decades as the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, it was finally built by MMRDA and opened in January 2024. It is India's longest bridge, and it shortens the trip between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai to around 20 minutes, giving quicker access to the Jawaharlal Nehru Port, the Mumbai–Pune Expressway and the new Navi Mumbai airport area.
facts: India's longest bridge, and its longest sea bridge, at about 21.8 km.
About 16.5 km of the bridge runs over the sea.
Cuts the Sewri–Chirle crossing to roughly 20 minutes.
One of the first roads in India to use open-road tolling, so vehicles don't stop at a toll gate.
Uses long steel deck spans so ships can pass safely beneath.

sources.title: MMRDA — Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority
